Yes, I know exactly where that is from.

That is a famous and controversial quote attributed to a 19-year-old **Mark Zuckerberg**.

It comes from an instant message conversation he had with a friend in 2004, shortly after he launched "Thefacebook.com" in his Harvard dorm room. He was describing the amount of personal data Harvard students were willingly handing over to his new website.

The full, and more damning, version of the exchange is:

> **Zuckerberg:** Yeah so if you ever need info about anyone at Harvard
> **Zuckerberg:** Just ask
> **Zuckerberg:** I have over 4,000 emails, pictures, addresses, SNS
>
> **[Friend]:** what? how'd you manage that one?
>
> **Zuckerberg:** people just submitted it
> **Zuckerberg:** i don't know why
> **Zuckerberg:** they "trust me"
> **Zuckerberg:** **dumb fucks**

This exchange has been used for years as a prime example by critics who argue that, from the very beginning, Zuckerberg had a cavalier and cynical attitude toward user privacy.
